analysis.overall: You had a solid day with 78% time in range and a beautifully steady night, though both main meals triggered sharp spikes over 200 mg/dL that required follow-up insulin.

events.title: Early afternoon low
events.description: Glucose drifted down to a brief low of 68 mg/dL before quickly bouncing back right before lunch.

events.title: Post-lunch surge
events.description: A 50g carb meal coming right off the low pushed levels up to 206 mg/dL, though insulin brought it back into target within an hour.

events.title: Extended dinner rise
events.description: Carbs from dinner caused a slow-building high peaking at 234 mg/dL, taking multiple small corrections before finally coming down overnight.

events.title: Smooth overnight baseline
events.description: Blood sugar stayed in a textbook flat line between 80 and 100 mg/dL all through the night.

events.title: Breakfast spike and quick drop
events.description: A 35g morning meal led to a steep climb to 235 mg/dL, but a prompt follow-up bolus sent levels dropping straight back toward range.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Giving meal boluses a bit earlier before eating could help smooth out those fast post-meal spikes.
